The image shows a corn plant with severely dried/bleached leaves wrapping around the stalk in the mid-canopy region, while surrounding plants are healthy and green. The affected plant shows:

- Dried, tan-to-brown bleached leaf tissue, particularly on the flag leaf and surrounding leaves near the ear/tassel zone
- The stalk appears intact with the tassel still present
- A single plant affected among healthy neighbors
- The bleaching/drying appears to start from the leaf sheath/collar area and wraps around

Key observations:
- The dark coloration visible at the leaf collar/sheath area where the dried tissue meets the stalk
- Purple/dark lesions at the stalk and leaf collar region with tan-brown dried tissue above
- Scattered occurrence (one plant affected among healthy ones)
- Tassel debris present at the leaf collar

This pattern, with dark lesions at the stalk/collar and pieces of tassel debris causing browning/death of the leaf sheath and surrounding leaf tissue, matches **Purple_Leaf_Sheath** very well. The symptom description states: "dark lesions on corn stalks and leaf collars, with color varying from purple to brown to black. Affected plants are scattered and random throughout the field" and "pieces of tassel debris fallen into the leaf collar are present in almost all cases."

The single affected plant surrounded by healthy green plants, combined with the dark collar lesions and dried bleached tissue, fits this diagnosis closely.
